style="font-family:inherit;font-size:7pt;">1</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:9pt;">Represents the rate at which a pool of mortgage loans' remaining balance is prepaid each month. The rate is calculated on an</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:9pt;">annualized basis and expressed as a percentage of the outstanding principal balance.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;">Changes in Mortgage Servicing Rights Valuation</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;"></font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">The decrease in the fair value of our MSRs during the </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">year ended December 31, 2015</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#32;was driven primarily</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">by the decrease in market interest rates and flattening of the yield curve during the year.  The key assumptions used in the estimation of the fair value of MSRs include prepayment speeds, discount rates, default rates, cost to service, contractual servicing fees, escrow earnings and ancillary income. The shape of the forward yield curve also has an impact on the asset </font></div><br><div style="text-align:center;"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#32;49</font></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div></div><br><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">valuation. We believe that the use of the forward yield curve better presents fair value of MSRs because the forward yield curve is the market&#8217;s expectation of future interest rates based on its expectation of inflation and other economic conditions.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">The spread between the weighted average coupon and current market rates determines modeled prepayment speed.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">During the </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">year ended December 31, 2015</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">, the weighted average coupon of our MSRs portfolio remained flat in</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">comparison to </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">December&#160;31, 2014</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#32;and, at </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">December&#160;31, 2015</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">, mortgage rates were lower during the </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">year ended December 31, 2015</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#32;than they were at during the year ended </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">December&#160;31, 2014</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">. The combination of these factors increased current prepayment estimates and prepayment estimates in the interest rate shifts.  The weighted average coupon of our MSRs portfolio also remained flat during the </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">year ended December 31, 2014</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#32;and mortgage rates were lower in comparison to rates at December 31, 2013.  Please see our disclosures in the "Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosure About Market Risk" section of this Management's Discussion and Analysis for further details on how interest rate fluctuations impact our MSRs valuation and the sensitivity of the yield curve. </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">The decrease was also driven by realized losses related to sales of mortgage servicing rights during the </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">year ended December 31, 2015</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#32;of $7,034, primarily related to 1) the change in fair value of the underlying MSRs from the time of the transaction bid to the date the assets are derecognized; 2) estimated prepayment protection provisions; and 3) costs associated with the sales. During the </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">year ended December 31, 2014</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">, we realized a gain on sale of MSRs of $1,082, net of protection provisions and transaction costs. </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;">Payoffs and Principal Amortization of Mortgage Servicing Rights Portfolio</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;"></font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">Payoffs and principal amortization of our MSRs portfolio related to our Servicing segment represents the value of our portfolio run-off, including paid off loans. and Stonegate&#8217;s cost basis in acquiring/producing those loans, including loan discount</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">fees, lender credits, yield spread premiums and servicing release premiums paid to correspondents. These items represent the</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">components that factor into the pricing of the loans to borrowers and represent the core &#8220;margin&#8221; elements of the loan sales.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;">Capitalized servicing rights - </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">An originated mortgage loan inherently includes both the value of the coupon to the</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">borrower as well as the servicing fee component to compensate the servicer for its activities. A key element of Stonegate&#8217;s</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">strategy is to retain the servicing of its loans upon sale to investors in order to take advantage of the value of the servicing</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">component. When Stonegate sells its loans &#8220;servicing retained&#8221;, a contractual separation of the servicing component occurs</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">from the underlying mortgage loan. This results in the creation of an MSRs asset. As such, a component of the gain on</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">mortgage loans held for sale is attributable to the creation of this MSRs asset and is based on the fair value of such MSRs asset</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">at the time of its creation (i.e. upon separation from the underlying loan during the loan sale). The Company utilizes a third-party analytic tool to derive/estimate this initial MSRs fair value at the time of sale.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;">Economic hedge results - </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">Unrealized gains/losses on loans not yet sold and accounted for under the fair value option</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">are included as a component of Gains on mortgage loans held for sale, net. This includes the impact of recording such loans at</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">fair value and the change from period to period based on market conditions. In addition, the change in value of Stonegate&#8217;s</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">interest rate lock commitments ("IRLCs") and other loan-related derivatives are recorded in this financial statement line item. We also enter into forward sales of MBS securities linked to security issuances of GSEs (FNMA, FHLMC, GNMA) for economic hedging purposes, as these instruments have similar characteristics to the loans held for sale by Stonegate. </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;">Provision for repurchase/indemnification obligation - </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">Stonegate makes certain representations and warranties to its</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">investors and insurers on loans sold. In the event of a breach of these reps and warranties, the Company may incur losses and/</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">or be required to repurchase loans from the investor. A provision is made at the time of sale for an estimate of such expected</font></div><br><div style="text-align:center;"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#32;56</font></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><a name="s94EF52DC836D91CE91A4F2182BE5E0B7"></a><div></div><br><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">losses, the amount of which is offset against this gain line item.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;">Direct loan origination costs - </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">Stonegate offsets its gains/losses on mortgage loans held for sale, as described by the</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">various categories above, with certain direct loan origination costs. These direct costs primarily relate to the following two</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">circumstances:</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">i) &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;Costs directly associated with the origination of the mortgage loans that are paid to/incurred with a third party</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:96px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">and are largely mandated by the investors as requirements for the loans to be sold. Such costs include net</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:96px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">appraisal fees, credit report fees, document preparation and imaging, risk management and loan file review</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:96px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">and certain FNMA/FHLMC/GNMA specific fees.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">ii) &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;Costs directly associated with the contractual creation of the separate servicing component of the loans upon</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:96px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">sale to the investors on a &#8220;servicing retained&#8221; basis. Such costs include the one-time upfront setup fees for</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:96px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">life of loan tax services (including tracking and paying of tax payments to jurisdictions), fees paid to an</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:96px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">outsource provider for valuation of initial MSRs created upon sale of the loan, and upfront recording fees at</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-indent:96px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">initial servicing setup.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;">Loan Origination and Other Loan Fees</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">Our loan origination and other loan fees during the </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">year ended December 31, 2014</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#32;increased </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">$2,997</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">, or </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">14%</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">,</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">compared to the comparable period in </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">2013</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">, due to higher origination volume and a higher mix of government insured loans,</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">which have higher margins than conventional mortgages, and an increase in retail originations, which also have higher margins than correspondent originations. However, our loan origination and other loan fees have decreased as a percentage of total originations to </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">20</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#32;bps from </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">24</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#32;bps for the </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">year ended December 31, 2014</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#32;and </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">2013</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">, respectively, due to the qualified mortgage rules effective January 2014, which limit the total fees allowed to be charged per transaction, but were offset by improved pricing margins. style="font-family:inherit;font-size:7pt;">1</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:9pt;">Represents the rate at which a pool of mortgage loans' remaining balance is prepaid each month. The rate is calculated on an</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:9pt;">annualized basis and expressed as a percentage of the outstanding principal balance.</font></div><br><div style="text-align:center;"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#32;59</font></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div></div><br><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:center;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;">Changes in Mortgage Servicing Rights Valuation</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">The decrease in the fair value of our MSRs was driven primarily by the decrease in market interest rates and flattening</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">of the yield curve during the latter part of 2014. Decreasing interest rates generally result in decreased MSRs values as the</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">assumption for prepayment speeds of the underlying mortgage loans tends to increase (mortgage loans prepay faster) and a</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">flattening yield curve decreases the expected value of interest income from the escrow balances held by us.  The decrease in the fair value of our MSRs was partially offset by a recognized gain on sale of mortgage servicing rights of $1,082 during the year ended </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">December&#160;31, 2014</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;">Payoffs and Principal Amortization of Mortgage Servicing Rights Portfolio</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">Payoffs and principal amortization of our MSRs portfolio related to our Servicing segment represents the value of our</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">portfolio run-off, including paid off loans.
